I am a **Postdoctoral Fellow** in the Digital Reskilling Lab at the **Harvard
Business School AI Institute** and a Research Affiliate of the Leibniz Institute
for Financial Research SAFE. Before joining HBS, I completed my PhD in Economics
at the Graduate School of Economics, Finance and Management at Goethe University
Frankfurt, supervised by Christine Laudenbach and Michael Kosfeld.

The rapid advance of artificial intelligence (AI) holds great promise for
improving efficiency and organizational decision-making, yet also raises profound
questions about transparency and the evolving role of human workers in modern
organizations. These tensions motivate my work: How can AI systems be implemented
responsibly to complement — rather than replace — human judgment and expertise?

In particular, I study how algorithmic design features, such as explainable AI,
shape human beliefs, (meta-)cognition, trust, and collaboration across different
stakeholder groups (direct users, service providers and consumers).

I approach these questions from a behavioral, individual-level perspective,
combining theory-driven incentivized experiments (online, lab-in-the-field,
field) with large-scale surveys, often in collaboration with industry partners in
real estate, banking, or fintech. A separate strand of work examines the
potential of evidence-based behavioral interventions to motivate debt repayment.
